forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 22%. Searches confirm no credible AGI announcement in the 1 day since prior forecast. Industry consensus remains split: Amodei (Anthropic) maintaining ~2027 AGI projection, Hassabis (DeepMind) at ~50% by 2030, Legg (DeepMind) at 50% for 'Minimal AGI' by 2028. Frontier model gains continue (Gemini 3.1 Pro 77.1% on ARC-AGI-2) but no resolution-triggering announcement.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: AI capability transitions predicted by experts within 5 years have historically materialised ~25-35% of the time within original timeframe. Adjusting downward for the very specific resolution criteria (formal lab announcement OR 3+ named researchers asserting AGI achieved).

factors_up.factor: Continued rapid frontier capability gains (Opus 4.6, Gemini 3.1 Pro ARC-AGI-2 doubling)
Anthropic CEO Amodei publicly forecasting AGI in 2027
Both labs claim models contributed materially to their own development
Massive capex sustaining training scale through 2029

factors_down.factor: Resolution requires explicit announcement vs marketing claims — high bar
Historical pattern of AI timelines slipping at the last 10%
Hassabis (DeepMind) consensus view of ~50% by 2030, not 2030 cutoff
Compute / energy constraints emerging 2027-2029

key_uncertainties: Definition of 'credible AGI announcement' vs marketing claims
Whether scaling laws hold past 2027 frontier
Whether 3+ researchers will publicly assert AGI achieved given social pressure
update_triggers: Major lab formal AGI declaration
Open letter from 3+ named researchers asserting AGI achieved
Sustained benchmark plateau >9 months
Saturation of ARC-AGI-2 or similar gatekeeper benchmarks

forecasts.question: Will economic consultancy lose ≥33% value/jobs by end 2030 due to AI?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 25%. McKinsey 2026 layoffs (~10% of global workforce, 3-4k positions) reinforce the headcount-contraction thesis. But BCG AI revenue at ~40% of 2026 revenue and Bain projecting 50% over coming years continues to point to a revenue-substitution rather than revenue-collapse pathway.
forecasts.base_rate: Industry-wide 33%+ revenue declines over 5-year periods are rare (<15% historically). Job declines of that magnitude have occurred in technology-disrupted sectors (~25% base rate).

factors_up.factor: McKinsey cutting ~10% of global workforce in 2026 attributed to AI
AI tools compressing analytical workflows from days to hours
Outcome-based pricing now ~25% of McKinsey fees — billable-hour model eroding

factors_down.factor: BCG AI revenue ~40% of 2026 revenue — substitution not destruction
Firms successfully repositioning as AI implementation partners
Demand for advisory on AI deployment expanding scope of work

key_uncertainties: Whether '33% decline' is measured by headcount or revenue
How rapidly clients move AI work in-house vs use consultancies
Whether boutique/specialist firms grow as Big 3 contract
update_triggers: Source Global Research / Kennedy report >20% sector revenue decline
Major firm announcing >20% workforce cut in one year
Big 3 firm winding down practice area

forecasts.question: Will Labour be largest party at next UK General Election?
forecasts.key_change: Slight uptick from 5 to 6%. May 2026 local elections cemented Reform's structural lead — Labour lost 208+ councillors and Reform gained 339 seats. But post-election polling showed only 5% of 2024 Labour voters switched to Reform vs 32% to Greens/Lib Dems, suggesting recoverable progressive bloc if Labour can reunite it under new leadership. Burnham succession scenario remains the most plausible recovery path.
forecasts.base_rate: Parties trailing by 8+ points 3 years before election win largest seat share ~15-20% historically; current FPTP fragmentation lowers Labour's seat-conversion efficiency.

factors_up.factor: Lost progressive vote went to Greens/Lib Dems (32%) not Reform — reclaimable
Burnham succession plausible; members 74% think Labour wins under him
Reform peaked at ~34% and has since declined to ~25-27%
3.5 years of horizon allows political volatility

factors_down.factor: May 2026 local elections devastated Labour (-208 councillors)
Reform UK leading polling at 26.9% with 188 projected seats
Labour at 18.7% national share, projected only 86 seats
Starmer leadership crisis ongoing, weak net favourability

key_uncertainties: Whether Labour replaces Starmer before 2027 and with whom
Whether Reform coalition holds or fragments
Whether progressive vote consolidates back to Labour vs Greens
update_triggers: Starmer resignation or successful leadership challenge
Sustained Labour polling above 25%
Reform internal split or major scandal

forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2035?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 79%. Long-horizon forecast unchanged in 1 day. Continued capability gains and majority of researcher surveys clustering around 2030-2035 timelines keep this above the 75% threshold.
forecasts.base_rate: Researcher surveys (2025-2026) cluster median AGI estimates around 2032-2035. Conditional on continued scaling, base rate for the horizon ~70-80%.

factors_up.factor: 9.5 year horizon accommodates multiple capability transitions
Frontier model gains continue (ARC-AGI-2 doubling year-over-year)
Major labs structurally pursuing AGI as primary objective
Researcher median timelines now mostly within window

factors_down.factor: Compute and energy constraints could plateau frontier
Regulatory or geopolitical shocks could decelerate
Definitional drift — AGI bar may rise as capabilities rise

key_uncertainties: Whether scaling laws hold for next 2-3 orders of magnitude
Energy/compute frontier in 2028-2032
How resolution criteria are interpreted by 3+ researchers
update_triggers: Sustained benchmark plateau >18 months
Major lab publicly winding down AGI program
Open letter from 3+ named researchers asserting AGI achieved

forecasts.question: Will China initiate a military blockade or invasion of Taiwan before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 7%. Continued PLA exercises (December 2025 Justice Mission, May 2026 South China Sea / West Pacific submarine deployments) signal escalating posture but no kinetic threshold crossed. Wang Yi labelling Taiwan 'biggest risk factor' is rhetorical, not escalatory. Taiwan's $25B special defense budget raising defensive capacity moderately reduces invasion-window incentives.
forecasts.base_rate: Great-power initiated cross-strait blockade/invasion has 0% historical base rate in modern era. Naval blockade base rate across major powers <5% per 4-year window.

factors_up.factor: PLA conducting larger and more frequent rehearsal exercises
Wang Yi labelling Taiwan 'biggest risk factor' to Rubio
Submarine deployments around Philippines signal regional escalation

factors_down.factor: US 2026 Annual Threat Assessment: no fixed Chinese invasion timeline
Taiwan defensive budget +$25B raises Chinese cost expectations
China's economic softness reduces appetite for major war
PLA still not at full operational capability for amphibious assault

key_uncertainties: Whether Xi succession or internal politics drives risk-taking
Whether US-Taiwan military integration accelerates
Whether PLA reaches assessed readiness threshold pre-2027
update_triggers: PLA Navy exercise crossing median line and not withdrawing
Restrictions on Taiwanese maritime trade lasting >24hrs
Major US-PRC diplomatic break

forecasts.question: Will UK annual CPI inflation fall below 2.0% for at least one month before 1 January 2027?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 3%. April 2026 CPI print confirmed at 2.8%, down from 3.3% in March. BoE April MPR projects CPI rising further: 3.1% Q2, 3.3% Q3, with 'somewhat further' in Q4. HM Treasury survey of independent forecasters has Q4 CPI averaging ~3.5%. Path to sub-2% before January 2027 effectively requires a major demand shock or oil price collapse.
forecasts.base_rate: Inflation falling from 2.8% to <2.0% within 8 months while official forecasts show the opposite trajectory is rare (<10% historically).

factors_up.factor: Volatility — inflation has surprised to the downside before
Sharp fall in global energy prices could cut headline CPI quickly

factors_down.factor: BoE explicitly projects CPI rising through Q2-Q4 2026
HM Treasury panel median 3.5% in Q4 2026
Sticky services inflation around 4%
Energy price floor from Middle East tensions

key_uncertainties: Whether oil prices fall sharply in H2 2026
How quickly base effects normalise in late 2026
Whether labour market loosens enough to cut services CPI
update_triggers: Monthly CPI surprise more than 0.4 pp below consensus
Sustained oil price decline below $60/bbl
BoE cutting forecasts materially in August 2026 MPR

forecasts.question: Will Spider-Man: Brand New Day gross over $1.5B worldwide by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 97%. Confirmed July 31, 2026 release. Trailer at 1B+ views, Polymarket 54.5% to be top-grossing 2026 domestic film. Pre-release tracking remains exceptional. Five months from release to year-end provides plenty of runway above $1.5B threshold (predecessor No Way Home reached $1.9B; this title has 1B-view trailer suggesting comparable or larger opening).
forecasts.base_rate: Of Spider-Man solo films post-2017, all three have grossed >$880M; Homecoming/Far From Home/No Way Home pattern with each entry's marketing performance suggesting Brand New Day tracks above $1.5B threshold.

factors_up.factor: 1B-view trailer (record-setting) signals enormous demand
Polymarket implied 54.5% to be top-grossing 2026 film
Five-month runway to December 31 leaves room for long tail
Strong predecessor (No Way Home at $1.9B worldwide)

factors_down.factor: China access uncertain — could cap international receipts
Avengers: Doomsday December 2026 release competes for late receipts
Unexpected reception risk

key_uncertainties: International box office split (China access)
Critical reception
Doomsday cannibalisation effect
update_triggers: Opening weekend below $200M domestic
Major China release decision
Significant critical backlash

forecasts.question: Will OpenAI and Anthropic have a combined ARR exceeding $70B by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 99%. Threshold already cleared at current reporting: Anthropic ~$45B ARR (May 2026), OpenAI ~$33B = ~$78B combined. Anthropic projecting first quarterly operating profit ($559M) in Q2 2026 on $10.9B revenue. Only material risk is dramatic accounting restatement (e.g. moving Anthropic to net-revenue basis would cut ~$8B) or year-end business shock.
forecasts.base_rate: Hardly any reference class — already-met financial thresholds with ongoing growth resolve YES with very high frequency (>95%).

factors_up.factor: Combined ARR already ~$78B in May 2026 reporting
Anthropic projecting Q2 quarterly operating profit
Both companies on steep growth trajectories

factors_down.factor: Accounting restatement risk (Anthropic gross vs net reporting) ~$8B swing
Macro/AI demand shock could decelerate Q4 ARR

key_uncertainties: Whether reporting standard shifts (gross vs net)
Whether market events trigger ARR decline by Q4
What 'credible reporting' means for resolution
update_triggers: Anthropic restated revenue to net basis
Major OpenAI funding round revising ARR claims
Significant Q3 2026 revenue miss

forecasts.question: Will UK average annual real GDP growth exceed 1.5% across the 2030s (2030-2039)?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 38%. OBR March 2026 EFO shows real GDP per capita averaging 1.1% growth 2026-2030 and headline growth ~1.6% through 2030. Productivity assumed to recover to 1% medium-term but population ageing weighing on labour supply growth (down to 0.5% by 2030). Achieving 1.5% average across full 2030s requires sustained productivity revival including 2032-2039 where uncertainty is highest.
forecasts.base_rate: UK 10-year average real GDP growth has exceeded 1.5% in roughly half of comparable rolling decades since 1970, but trend has weakened post-2008. Productivity-conditional base rate ~35-40%.

factors_up.factor: OBR projecting growth ~1.6% through 2030 — slightly above threshold
Productivity recovery to 1% assumed medium-term
AI productivity upside not yet priced into OBR projections

factors_down.factor: Population ageing reducing labour supply growth to 0.5% by 2030
Real GDP per capita only 1.1% — implies weak total growth without migration
Net migration declining structurally
Productivity has missed forecasts persistently since 2010

key_uncertainties: Whether AI delivers productivity step-change in 2030s
Net migration policy through 2030s
Fiscal space for investment under demographic pressure
update_triggers: Sustained productivity growth above 1.2% for 2+ years
Major AI adoption studies showing GDP impact materialising
OBR revising medium-term growth assumptions upward
